note:
Tables defined BOTH by a runtime CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS in cloudflare-worker/src and by the SQL tree, whose two definitions do not declare the same columns. D1 holds one table per name and IF NOT EXISTS cannot add a column to a table that already exists, so whichever runs first wins and a column only the loser declares never exists.

WHICH SIDE WINS IS DECIDED BY PROVISIONING ORDER, AND IT WAS MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSUMED. `migrate-d1 --bootstrap` loads schema_baseline.sql and then every post-cutoff migration, and branch-provision.yml runs it BEFORE `wrangler deploy` — so on any database this repo's own tooling creates, the SQL side lands before a request can reach a route and every runtime CREATE is a no-op. Built against a fresh build, 27 of the 29 pairs below have a runtime definition whose columns are all present; only capital_calls and oauth_state_tokens declare a runtime column the resulting database lacks. That is why this list is a ledger of stale bootstraps rather than a list of live 500s.

SIX OF THEM ARE ALREADY BEHIND THEIR OWN READERS, which is the sharpest thing this gate found: monitoring_analytics.ts, advisor.ts, brand.ts (twice), legalcap.ts and settings.ts each bootstrap a table and then query a column that bootstrap does not create. On a database where the bootstrap ran first those files break themselves. Each is named in its entry.

PARTNER_PROFILES IS NOT ON THIS LIST, AND THAT IS THE GATE'S OWN FIRST PROOF. D187's three-way collision is fully converged: routes/profiling.ts's 24-entry ADD COLUMN loop reaches migration 275's shape exactly. It appeared here as a one-column superset until the stale-entry refusal caught the cause — this gate's pair parser was dropping `['raw_chat_json', "TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'"]`, because a quote inside a differently-quoted literal is content and the character class it used could not know that.

The gate fails on NEW entries and on entries here whose definitions now agree, so this list cannot go stale. Resolving one means widening the narrow definition — usually by adding the columns to the ALTER list beside its CREATE, which is what D187 did for partner_profiles — and deleting its line.
resolve_with: npx wrangler d1 execute studioos-db --remote --command="PRAGMA table_info('<table>')"

pairs.divergent:capital_calls: TWO INCOMPATIBLE SHAPES, AND ONE OF THE TWO CAPITAL-CALL PATHS IS DEAD. routes/legalcap.ts:73 creates (deal_id, syndicate_id, amount_cents, currency, lp_responses, notes, idempotency_key, created_by, updated_at); the baseline creates (uid, limited_partner_id, lp_investor_id, project_id, amount, paid_date). Neither is a subset. A fresh build carries the BASELINE shape, so legalcap.ts's nine columns exist nowhere — and legalcap.ts's own ten statements on this table name syndicate_id and lp_responses, so they throw. Already on record in sqlite-table-collisions-baseline.json, which reaches the same verdict from the mutual-fatality side; resolving it is a decision about which capital-call path survives, not a rename, and belongs to that ledger's entry.
pairs.divergent:oauth_state_tokens: THREE DEFINITIONS, AND calendar.ts KNOWS IT LOST — its own comment says so. integrations/oauth.ts:26 creates (state PK, user_id, provider, pkce_verifier, extra_json, created_at, consumed_at); routes/calendar.ts:105 creates (id AUTOINCREMENT, state UNIQUE, user_id, provider, expires_at, created_at) and then ALTERs expires_at in 'if the table existed in the integrations/oauth.ts shape'. The baseline is oauth.ts's shape plus that expires_at, so oauth.ts won and calendar.ts's self-heal is what production ran. The one column a fresh build lacks is calendar.ts's `id`, and NOTHING reads it: every statement across calendar.ts, fundSheets.ts, oauth.ts, salesforce.ts, carta.ts and docusign.ts keys on `state`. The one consequence the divergence DID have is fixed in this same change — see D191 and calendar.ts:130, where the sweep had been deleting every row oauth.ts wrote.
pairs.refused:project_metrics: A BOOTSTRAP REAL SQLITE REFUSES, SO IT HAS NEVER RUN. integrations/providers/stripe.ts:329 writes created_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime("now")) with DOUBLE quotes; SQLite rejects that with 'default value of column [created_at] is not constant' whether or not double-quoted string literals are enabled, and the statement's own `catch { /* table exists */ }` has been swallowing the proof. Harmless today and only today: migration 249 and routes/progress.ts:1842 both create project_metrics with datetime('now'), they agree with each other, and a fresh build carries that shape — so the table the refused CREATE would have made already exists. Fixing the two characters is filed rather than done here, with metric_anomalies, whose sole definition fails the same way and which therefore does NOT exist.
pairs.interpolated:explorer_promo_codes: NOT ANALYSABLE, AND RECORDED RATHER THAN SKIPPED. services/explorerPromo.ts:75 builds its CREATE TABLE through a template literal carrying a ${…}, so no column set can be read from it without executing the module. The other definition is the baseline's. Silently dropping a definition the gate cannot build is how a gate comes to report a pass over a corpus it never read, so it is a finding kind of its own; closing it means making the statement literal.
pairs.superset:activity_logs: routes/partnernet.ts:99 bootstraps a five-column activity_logs (id, user_id, type, meta, created_at) while the baseline's own shape adds uid, project_id, action, details, actor, latency_ms, status_code, endpoint and method — the columns middleware/observability.ts writes on every request. partnernet.ts's own six statements name none of the nine, so it is narrow rather than wrong, and a fresh build carries the wide shape. It is a self-heal for a table that predates the migration set and has not been revisited since.
pairs.superset:admin_audit_log: THREE DEFINITIONS, AND THE NARROW ONE READS WHAT IT DOES NOT CREATE. routes/admin.ts:458 and the baseline agree; routes/monitoring_analytics.ts:83 lacks viewed_user_id, conversation_id, viewed_at and actor — and its own eleven statements on this table name viewed_user_id, so on a database where that bootstrap ran first the D157 self-service audit read throws. A fresh build carries the wide shape, so it is inert on every provisioned database. Closing it means bringing monitoring_analytics.ts's CREATE up to admin.ts's, or deleting it in favour of services/adminAudit.ts's ensureAdminAuditLogTable.
pairs.superset:advisor_messages: routes/advisor.ts:174 bootstraps advisor_messages without safety_score or sanitisation_actions_json, which migration 043 added — and the same file's three statements on the table name BOTH of them. So advisor.ts's own guardrail write depends on a column advisor.ts's own CREATE does not declare. A fresh build has both, so the guardrail audit works everywhere it matters; the bootstrap is a 043-era self-heal nobody widened.
pairs.superset:cohort_cycles: services/cohortTiming.ts:177 creates the cycle row without applications_open_at, applications_close_at, app_status or force_proceed — migration 157's application-window columns. The reader is a different file (services/cohortApplications.ts, plus routes/admin_cohort.ts:439 for force_proceed), and cohortTiming.ts's own ten statements name none of the four, so the two files split cleanly: one owns the calendar, the other owns the window. A fresh build carries all four.
pairs.superset:esign_envelopes: THREE DEFINITIONS. routes/esign.ts:55 and the baseline agree; services/trustEnvelope.ts:78 lacks provider, docusign_envelope_id, docusign_account_id and last_error — migration 021's DocuSign columns. trustEnvelope.ts's one statement on the table names none of them, and the DocuSign readers all live in integrations/providers/docusign.ts, so the narrow bootstrap is a trust-flow safety net that predates the provider split. A fresh build carries the wide shape.
pairs.superset:investor_dealroom_members: middleware/requireInvestorTier.ts:182 bootstraps the table without company_id, which migration 193 added for company scoping. That middleware runs no statement against the table at all — it creates it so the tier gate's later reads cannot 'no such table' — and the company_id readers are middleware/activeCompany.ts and services/tenancyScope.ts. A fresh build has the column.
pairs.superset:investor_introductions: The same one-column gap as investor_dealroom_members and from the same file: middleware/requireInvestorTier.ts:168 creates investor_introductions without migration 193's company_id. Zero statements on the table in that file; the readers are activeCompany.ts and tenancyScope.ts. A fresh build has it. The two entries stay separate because a guard that merged them would stop naming which CREATE to widen.
pairs.superset:investor_profiles: routes/investor_signals.ts:57 lacks deal_volume_band, coinvest_pref_text and watchlist_seed_text — the three columns migration 276 landed for D188 after migration 042 declared them and never applied them. investor_signals.ts's own six statements name none of the three; the reader is services/advisor/writeRouter.ts. A fresh build has all three, which is what D188 was for.
pairs.superset:landing_pages: THREE DEFINITIONS AND THE WIDEST READER IS THE NARROWEST WRITER. migration 144's rebuild (and the migrations after it, to 48 columns) is the shape a fresh build carries. routes/brand.ts:42 creates 19 columns and then runs 38 statements on the table that name ALL 29 it does not create — every audience_* field, template, goal, content_json, preview_token. services/advisor/writeRouter.ts:986 creates 16 and reads none of the rest. So brand.ts's whole multi-page brand site depends on columns its own bootstrap has never created; it works because the migration always lands first. This is the clearest case in the ledger for widening the CREATE rather than trusting the order.
pairs.superset:legal_documents: routes/legalcap.ts:39 creates legal_documents without fund_id, which the baseline's own shape carries for the fund LPA. legalcap.ts's five statements on the table name none of it; the fund_id reader is routes/funds.ts, which D174 repointed. A fresh build has the column.
pairs.superset:metrics_snapshots: routes/pipeline.ts:55 creates the deal-shaped metrics_snapshots without the ten metric columns migration 173 ALTERs in (arr, cac, ltv, monthly_churn_pct, new_users, net_burn, cash_balance, headcount, nrr_pct, paying_accounts). pipeline.ts's own four statements name none of them. This is the table of #183/#202 and of sqlite-table-collisions-baseline.json's longest entry; what remains after those two is only this width gap, because the incompatible project_id shape has been retired from every live definition.
pairs.superset:mvp_tasks: routes/pipeline.ts:41 creates mvp_tasks without `lane`, which migration 253 added for the board columns. pipeline.ts's own four statements do not name it; the reader is routes/founder_board.ts. A fresh build has it.
pairs.superset:notifications_inbox: FOUR DEFINITIONS, THREE OF THEM IN AGREEMENT. services/email/send.ts:152, services/notify.ts:74 and the baseline all carry migration 053's category, severity, cta_url and template_key — send.ts and notify.ts through their own ALTER loops, which is the pattern this gate has to resolve to see them agree. routes/notifications.ts:107 lacks all four and names none of them in its own eight statements. A fresh build has them; the odd one out is the read route's safety net.
pairs.superset:pairwise_ndas: services/trust.ts:139 creates pairwise_ndas without signers_json, voided_at or voided_reason, which the baseline carries. Its own five statements on the table name none of the three, and the void path lives in routes/trust.ts. A fresh build has them.
pairs.superset:subsidiaries: THE NARROW DEFINITION READS ALL SIX COLUMNS IT DOES NOT CREATE. routes/legalcap.ts:55 bootstraps subsidiaries without spinout_status, ip_license_doc_id, equity_allocation_json, stripe_atlas_id, independent_scaling_enabled or post_spinout_dashboard_url — and its own twenty-two statements on the table name every one of them. So the spin-out surface in that file is entirely dependent on the baseline landing first. A fresh build carries all six; widening the CREATE is what closes this.
pairs.superset:user_google_links: routes/calendar.ts:893 creates user_google_links without created_at, which the baseline carries. Its own five statements do not name it. A one-column gap in a self-heal for the OAuth link row; a fresh build has it.
pairs.superset:user_profile_ext: services/profileExpansion.ts:860 creates user_profile_ext without `organization`, added by migration 180. Its own two statements on the table do not name it — the reader is routes/settings.ts. A fresh build has it.
pairs.superset:user_sessions: THE NARROW DEFINITION READS ALL FOUR COLUMNS IT DOES NOT CREATE, AND THEY ARE THE STEP-UP COLUMNS. routes/settings.ts:110 bootstraps user_sessions without factor, last_step_up_at, step_up_due_at or assurance_level — migration 011's SMS-2FA set and the step-up columns on top of it — while its own five statements on the table name every one of them. On a database where that CREATE ran first, settings.ts's own session list and revoke throw. A fresh build has all four, so this is inert everywhere it is provisioned; it is the entry most worth closing, because the columns are auth state.
pairs.superset:user_skills: services/skillProfileSchema.ts:21 creates user_skills without taxonomy_version, which the baseline carries. Its one statement on the table does not name it; the reader is services/skillsTaxonomySchema.ts. A fresh build has it.
pairs.superset:user_values: The same one-column gap as user_skills, on its sibling table and from the other file: services/skillsTaxonomySchema.ts:105 creates user_values without taxonomy_version. That file runs no statement against user_values at all. A fresh build has it.
pairs.superset:waitlist_signups: routes/brand.ts:80 creates waitlist_signups without audience, crm_status, invited_at, followed_up_at, promoted_at or promoted_interview_id — migration 081's audience column and the CRM set after it — and its own four statements on the table name `audience`. So the landing-page signup write depends on a column its own bootstrap omits. A fresh build has all six. This is brand.ts's second entry in this ledger, after landing_pages.
pairs.superset:wellbeing_resources: routes/wellbeing.ts:105 creates wellbeing_resources without updated_at, which the baseline carries. Its own six statements do not name it. Note this table also appears in sqlite-table-collisions-baseline.json for a different reason — an archived `title`-requiring shape — and the two entries are about different definitions: that one is the schema files disagreeing, this one is the live bootstrap being one column narrow.
pairs.superset:workflow_tasks: services/workflowSchema.ts:51 creates workflow_tasks without assigned_to, sort_order or updated_at, which the baseline carries. That file runs no statement against the table; the readers are in routes/workflows.ts. A fresh build has all three.
pairs.superset:workflows: services/workflowSchema.ts:30 creates workflows without updated_at, which the baseline carries. Its own two statements on the table do not name it. Kept separate from workflow_tasks because the two CREATEs are separate statements in that file and each has to be widened on its own.
